title: Islam: giving
hookLine: a set share of wealth goes each year to those in need

cards: A coin in the cup, when there's one in a pocket. A fundraiser link, tapped because a friend shared it. Giving like that is nice, occasional, optional.
Zakat works more like rent. Once a year, a Muslim with enough savings sits down with a calculator, adds them up, and a set share goes to people in need. Not whenever the mood strikes.
Every year, on a schedule, as part of the faith.

teach.b: Zakat is the third pillar of Islam, after the shahada and the prayer; in the Qur'an, the command to pray and the command to give zakat often come in the same breath. Here's how it works.

teach.h: A SET SHARE, ONCE A YEAR.
teach.b: If a Muslim's savings stay above a minimum amount, called the nisab, for a full lunar year, they give a portion, by long tradition two and a half percent, to those in need.
Islamic law works out the details for gold, crops, livestock and trade goods.
The Qur'an names who can receive it, including the poor, the needy, people in debt, travelers stranded far from home, and those working to free captives. Now the word itself.
The Qur'an says to the Prophet, in Marmaduke Pickthall's 1930 translation: "Take alms of their wealth, wherewith thou mayst purify them and mayst make them grow."
Purify and grow: the two ideas the word zakat carries. And purify them: not the money, the people. Giving cleans the giver's heart of greed and the fear of not having enough.

A hadith in Sahih Muslim says charity never decreases wealth. Beside zakat, which is required, there's sadaqah, voluntary giving, which can be anything; a hadith counts even a smile to your brother as sadaqah.

teach.h: ZAKAT THE FLOOR, SADAQAH NO CEILING.
teach.b: Zakat is the floor, set and dependable; sadaqah has no ceiling.
Some Muslims time their zakat for Ramadan, and there is a special gift of food before the prayer at the end of Ramadan, so everyone can celebrate.

how: Muslims whose savings exceed the nisab for a lunar year give zakat, usually two and a half percent, directly or through mosques and charities; some pay it in Ramadan, and zakat al-fitr is given before the Eid prayer.

o: a set yearly share of savings for those in need
a pilgrimage to Mecca made once in a lifetime
a gift given whenever you happen to feel moved

games.q: the Qur'an says alms purify. who, or what, gets purified?
games.why: Qur'an 9:103: take alms of their wealth, wherewith thou mayst purify them. the giving cleans the giver's heart.

practice: Notice what you have more than enough of: money, maybe, but also time, food in the cupboard, clothes you don't wear, attention.
Choose one thing, and one person or cause it could go to, and notice any tightness as you picture giving it away. That tightness is what the word zakat is about.

wordCard.voice: Zakat. A set share of wealth given each year to those in need, named for purifying and growing. The third pillar. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: purification, growth; the obligatory alms.
